As the code stands, `deposit()` reverts on every call against\nthe real USDT at `0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7`, so the vault would go\nlive and immediately accept nothing. That failure is load-bearing for everything else:\nit means the contract has never been executed against its own underlying asset, and the\n39 green tests do not tell you otherwise.\n\nIf you fix only that one line, you ship a vault that pays depositors **0% yield**,\nstrands every dollar of Aave interest in a contract with no recovery function, and lets\nthe owner key take a pending deposit almost in full. Those are separate defects and each\none is demonstrated below.\n\nNothing under `src/` was modified. `test/UsdtYieldVault.t.sol` and `test/mocks/` are\nuntouched. All new code is in `test/audit/`, `test/harness/` and `test/fork/`.\n\n---\n\n## Contents\n\n| # | Severity | Finding |\n|---|---|---|\n| [F-1](#f-1) | Critical | `deposit()` always reverts against real USDT — the vault is inoperable on mainnet |\n| [F-2](#f-2) | Critical | Aave yield is never credited and is permanently unrecoverable; depositors end up poorer |\n| [F-3](#f-3) | High | The withdrawal fee is destroyed, not redistributed — contradicts the README |\n| [F-4](#f-4) | Critical | Owner can front-run and confiscate a pending deposit; deposit fee is uncapped |\n| [F-5](#f-5) | High | `pause()` freezes withdrawals of money already deposited; `renounceOwnership()` makes it permanent |\n| [F-6](#f-6) | Medium | Dust withdrawals burn shares for zero USDT locally, and revert inside real Aave |\n| [F-7](#f-7) | Medium | `deposit()` re-approves without zeroing; real USDT rejects non-zero → non-zero allowance changes |\n| [F-8](#f-8) | Low (latent) | USDT's transfer-fee switch would short-change the vault; no defence |\n| [F-9](#f-9) | Low | Constructor takes no validation; `aUsdt` is dead state; event semantics inconsistent |\n\nPlus [why the 39 tests and 100% coverage missed all of this](#why-the-green-tick-was-empty).\n\n---\n\n## How to reproduce\n\nEverything except `test/fork/` runs offline:\n\n```bash\nforge test --no-match-path \"test/fork/*\"\n```\n\nThe fork tests hit mainnet at a pinned block and need an archive endpoint. They default\nto `https://eth.drpc.org`, which served block 25,600,000 when I ran them; override with\nyour own if you prefer:\n\n```bash\nforge test --match-path \"test/fork/*\" -vv\n# or\nMAINNET_RPC_URL=https://your-endpoint forge test --match-path \"test/fork/*\" -vv\n```\n\n**Almost every test I added is written to fail.** Each one asserts a property the\ncontract is supposed to have, so the failure message *is* the evidence. A handful named\n`test_Report_*` / `test_Fork_Report_*` pass on purpose — those measure the size of a\nproblem rather than assert a property, and they are labelled as such below.\n\n### Files added\n\n| File | Purpose |\n|---|---|\n| `test/harness/NonStandardUsdt.sol` | Local USDT with mainnet TetherToken semantics (no return values, allowance guard, fee switch) |\n| `test/harness/AccruingAavePool.sol` | Aave pool stand-in whose aToken actually rebases, like real aUSDT |\n| `test/harness/SafeAavePool.sol` | Aave pool stand-in that moves tokens with SafeERC20 and rejects zero withdrawals, like real Aave |\n| `test/audit/RealUsdtCompat.t.sol` | F-1, F-7, F-8 offline |\n| `test/audit/Accounting.t.sol` | F-2, F-3 |\n| `test/audit/OwnerPowers.t.sol` | F-4, F-5 |\n| `test/audit/Rounding.t.sol` | F-6 |\n| `test/audit/Invariant.t.sol` | Stateful invariants quantifying F-2/F-3 |\n| `test/fork/MainnetUsdt.t.sol` | F-1, F-6, F-7 against the real mainnet contracts |\n\nThe three harness contracts exist because the repo's own mocks model neither of the two\nthings that matter: `MockUSDT` is a stock OpenZeppelin ERC20 (real USDT is not one), and\n`MockAavePool` mints a fixed-supply receipt token (real aUSDT rebases). I left both mocks\nin place as instructed and added new ones alongside.\n\n---\n\n<a name=\"f-1\"></a>\n## F-1 — Critical — `deposit()` always reverts against real USDT\n\n`src/UsdtYieldVault.sol:94`:\n\n```solidity\nusdt.approve(address(aavePool), amount);\n```\n\n`usdt` is typed `IERC20`, whose `approve` is declared `returns (bool)`. Solidity therefore\nemits an ABI decode of 32 bytes of return data after the call. Mainnet USDT (TetherToken)\ndeclares `function approve(address _spender, uint _value) public` — **no return value**.\nThe call itself succeeds and returns zero bytes; the decode then reverts.\n\nThe vault pulls the user's USDT on line 93 and dies on line 94. Every deposit, every user,\nevery time. There is no code path into the vault that avoids this line.\n\n### Evidence — against the real token on a mainnet fork\n\n```\n$ forge test --match-path \"test/fork/MainnetUsdt.t.sol\" -vv\n\nRan 6 tests for test/fork/MainnetUsdt.t.sol:MainnetUsdtForkTest\n[FAIL: custom error 0x2c5211c6] test_Fork_AaveAcceptsZeroWithdraw() (gas: 440252)\n[FAIL: EvmError: Revert] test_Fork_DepositWorksOnMainnet() (gas: 332123)\n[PASS] test_Fork_Report_AusdtRebasesButTotalAssetsStoredCannot() (gas: 363186)\nLogs:\n  supplied to real Aave        : 100000000000\n  aUSDT after supply           : 99999999999\n  aUSDT after 365 days         : 102765734567\n  interest earned              : 2765734568\n  implied APY, bps             : 276\n\n[FAIL: raw approve failed] test_Fork_UsdtAllowsOverwritingNonZeroAllowance() (gas: 36918)\n[FAIL: mainnet USDT.approve returns no data; IERC20.approve decodes 32 bytes: 0 != 32] test_Fork_UsdtApproveReturnsABool() (gas: 39781)\nLogs:\n  raw call ok                  : true\n  return data length (bytes)   : 0\n\n[FAIL: EvmError: Revert] test_Fork_UsdtApproveThroughIerc20() (gas: 35078)\nSuite result: FAILED. 1 passed; 5 failed; 0 skipped; finished in 488.54ms (12.72ms CPU time)\n\nRan 1 test suite in 493.57ms (488.54ms CPU time): 1 tests passed, 5 failed, 0 skipped (6 total tests)\n```\n\n`test_Fork_UsdtApproveReturnsABool` is the root cause in one line: the raw call to real\nUSDT's `approve` **succeeds** (`raw call ok: true`) and returns **0 bytes**, where\n`IERC20.approve` requires 32.\n\nThe trace shows exactly where the vault dies — `transferFrom` lands, `approve` returns\n`[Stop]` with no data, and `deposit` reverts immediately after:\n\n```\n$ forge test --match-test test_Fork_DepositWorksOnMainnet -vvvv\n\n    ├─ [72874] UsdtYieldVault::deposit(10000000000 [1e10])\n    │   ├─ [34830] 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7::transferFrom(alice: [0x328809Bc894f92807417D2dAD6b7C998c1aFdac6], UsdtYieldVault: [0x5615dEB798BB3E4dFa0139dFa1b3D433Cc23b72f], 10000000000 [1e10])\n    │   │   ├─ emit Transfer(from: alice: [0x328809Bc894f92807417D2dAD6b7C998c1aFdac6], to: UsdtYieldVault: [0x5615dEB798BB3E4dFa0139dFa1b3D433Cc23b72f], value: 10000000000 [1e10])\n    │   │   └─ ← [Stop]\n    │   ├─ [24953] 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7::approve(0x87870Bca3F3fD6335C3F4ce8392D69350B4fA4E2, 10000000000 [1e10])\n    │   │   ├─ emit Approval(owner: UsdtYieldVault: [0x5615dEB798BB3E4dFa0139dFa1b3D433Cc23b72f], spender: 0x87870Bca3F3fD6335C3F4ce8392D69350B4fA4E2, value: 10000000000 [1e10])\n    │   │   └─ ← [Stop]\n    │   └─ ← [Revert] EvmError: Revert\n    └─ ← [Revert] EvmError: Revert\n\nBacktrace:\n  at UsdtYieldVault.deposit\n  at MainnetUsdtForkTest.test_Fork_DepositWorksOnMainnet\n```\n\nNote the addresses in that trace are the real ones from `README.md`: USDT\n`0xdAC17F9…D831ec7` and the Aave V3 pool `0x87870Bc…B4fA4E2`.\n\n### Evidence — offline, no network needed\n\n```\n$ forge test --match-path \"test/audit/RealUsdtCompat.t.sol\" -vv\n\nRan 4 tests for test/audit/RealUsdtCompat.t.sol:RealUsdtCompatTest\n[FAIL: EvmError: Revert] test_DepositWorksAgainstMainnetUsdtSemantics() (gas: 86972)\n[FAIL: unsafe approve] test_ReApprovingANonZeroAllowanceSucceeds() (gas: 38373)\n[PASS] test_Report_UsdtTransferFeeSwitchShortchangesTheVault() (gas: 121386)\nLogs:\n  amount passed to transfer    : 10000000000\n  amount actually received     : 9990000000\n  shortfall                    : 10000000\n\n[FAIL: USDT.approve returns nothing; IERC20.approve requires 32 bytes of bool: 0 != 32] test_UsdtApproveReturnsABool() (gas: 41574)\nLogs:\n  call succeeded               : true\n  return data length (bytes)   : 0\n\nSuite result: FAILED. 1 passed; 3 failed; 0 skipped; finished in 729.08µs (561.92µs CPU time)\n\nRan 1 test suite in 336.24ms (729.08µs CPU time): 1 tests passed, 3 failed, 0 skipped (4 total tests)\n```\n\n### Fix\n\nThe file already imports `SafeERC20` and uses it correctly for `safeTransferFrom` on line\n93 — line 94 is the one place it was skipped. Replace it with `forceApprove`, which\ntolerates missing return values *and* handles the zero-first requirement in F-7:\n\n```solidity\nusdt.forceApprove(address(aavePool), amount);\n```\n\n`using SafeERC20 for IERC20` is already declared on line 20, so this is a one-word change.\nSetting the allowance back to zero after `supply` returns (or approving `type(uint256).max`\nonce in the constructor) are both reasonable, but `forceApprove` per deposit is the\nsmallest correct change.\n\nDo not rely on `IERC20` for any other USDT call. `safeTransferFrom` on line 93 is already\ncorrect; there are no other direct token calls.\n\n---\n\n<a name=\"f-2\"></a>\n## F-2 — Critical — Aave yield is never credited, and is permanently unrecoverable\n\n`src/UsdtYieldVault.sol:143-145`:\n\n```solidity\nfunction totalAssets() public view returns (uint256) {\n    return totalAssetsStored;\n}\n```\n\n`totalAssetsStored` is a plain counter: it goes up by `amount` in `deposit()` and down by\n`grossAssets` in `withdraw()`. Nothing else writes it. Meanwhile the vault's actual\nposition is `aUsdt.balanceOf(address(this))`, which rebases upward continuously — that is\nthe entire reason for supplying to Aave.\n\nSince every share price calculation (`convertToShares`, `convertToAssets`,\n`balanceOfUnderlying`, `sharePrice`) is driven by `totalAssetsStored`, **no depositor can\never withdraw a cent of interest.** It accumulates as aUSDT owned by the vault.\n\nThere is no way to get it out. The only outbound call in the whole contract is:\n\n```\n$ grep -nE \"safeTransfer|\\.transfer\\(|withdraw\\(|sweep|rescue|skim\" src/UsdtYieldVault.sol\n93:        usdt.safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), amount);\n107:    function withdraw(uint256 shares) external whenNotPaused nonReentrant returns (uint256 netAssets) {\n119:        aavePool.withdraw(address(usdt), netAssets, msg.sender);\n```\n\nLine 119 is share-driven, and shares can only ever claim `totalAssetsStored`. There is no\nsweep, no rescue, no fee collector. The interest is gone.\n\nThe `aUsdt` immutable — the one piece of state that would fix this — is stored and never\nread:\n\n```\n$ grep -n \"aUsdt\" src/UsdtYieldVault.sol\n41:    IERC20 public immutable aUsdt;\n68:    /// @param _aUsdt The Aave aUSDT receipt token.\n72:    constructor(address _usdt, address _aUsdt, address _aavePool, uint256 _depositFeeBps, address initialOwner)\n76:        aUsdt = IERC20(_aUsdt);\n```\n\n### Evidence\n\n`test/harness/AccruingAavePool.sol` is an Aave stand-in whose aToken rebases the way real\naUSDT does (scaled balance × liquidity index). `pool.accrue(500)` pays 5% interest and\nbacks it with real underlying, exactly as Aave does.\n\n```\n$ forge test --match-path \"test/audit/Accounting.t.sol\" -vv\n\nRan 6 tests for test/audit/Accounting.t.sol:AccountingTest\n[FAIL: withdrawal fees are unrecoverable, not redistributed: 59999999 != 0] test_FeesAloneDoNotStrandValue() (gas: 372153)\nLogs:\n  totalShares                  : 0\n  aUSDT stranded in vault      : 59999999\n\n[FAIL: value left in Aave that no share can ever claim: 529999999 != 0] test_NoValueIsStrandedAfterEveryoneExits() (gas: 279565)\nLogs:\n  totalShares                  : 0\n  totalAssetsStored            : 0\n  aUSDT stranded in vault      : 529999999\n\n[PASS] test_Report_LeakOverOneYear() (gas: 359224)\nLogs:\n  aUSDT held by vault          : 21006495268\n  claimable by all shareholders: 19999999999\n  unclaimable                  : 1006495269\n  unclaimable, as bps of TVL   : 479\n\n[FAIL: depositor is poorer than before, despite the position earning 5%: 999970000000 < 1000000000000] test_SoleDepositorEarnsTheYield() (gas: 276400)\nLogs:\n  alice deposited              : 10000000000\n  alice got back after +5% APY : 9970000000\n  wallet before                : 1000000000000\n  wallet after                 : 999970000000\n\n[FAIL: totalAssets() ignores accrued Aave interest: 10000000000 != 10500000000] test_TotalAssetsTracksAaveBalance() (gas: 260371)\nLogs:\n  aUSDT actually held by vault : 10500000000\n  vault.totalAssets()          : 10000000000\n\n[FAIL: withdrawal fee was charged but credited to nobody: 1 !~= 30015007 (max delta: 1, real delta: 30015006)] test_WithdrawFeeAccruesToRemainingShareholders() (gas: 352699)\nLogs:\n  alice withdrawal fee charged : 30015007\n  bob claim before alice exited: 9994997498\n  bob claim after alice exited : 9994997499\n  bob actually gained          : 1\n\nSuite result: FAILED. 1 passed; 5 failed; 0 skipped; finished in 1.42ms (2.44ms CPU time)\n\nRan 1 test suite in 145.38ms (1.42ms CPU time): 1 tests passed, 5 failed, 0 skipped (6 total tests)\n```\n\nRead `test_SoleDepositorEarnsTheYield` carefully. Alice deposits 10,000 USDT. The position\nearns 5%. She withdraws everything and gets back **9,970 USDT**. She is 30 USDT poorer\nthan if she had done nothing at all, while 530 USDT of her money sits in Aave under the\nvault's address with no function that can move it.\n\n`test_Report_LeakOverOneYear` (passes, it is a measurement) puts a number on it: after one\nyear at ~5% on a 20,000 USDT deposit, **479 bps of TVL — 1,006 USDT — is unclaimable.**\nThat is the yield the product is named after.\n\nThe rate is not hypothetical. On the real Aave pool at the pinned block, USDT was paying\n276 bps and the aUSDT balance really does rebase — from the fork run in F-1:\n\n```\n  supplied to real Aave        : 100000000000\n  aUSDT after supply           : 99999999999\n  aUSDT after 365 days         : 102765734567\n  interest earned              : 2765734568\n  implied APY, bps             : 276\n```\n\n### Fix\n\nMake `totalAssets()` read the position instead of a stored counter:\n\n```solidity\nfunction totalAssets() public view returns (uint256) {\n    return aUsdt.balanceOf(address(this));\n}\n```\n\nThen delete `totalAssetsStored` and every write to it, and change `convertToShares` /\n`convertToAssets` / `sharePrice` to call `totalAssets()`. Note that `convertToShares` must\nread the balance *before* the new deposit is supplied, so keep the share calculation ahead\nof the `supply()` call as it is today.\n\nTwo things to get right while you are in there:\n\n- With a balance-driven `totalAssets()`, the vault becomes vulnerable to the classic\n  first-depositor donation/inflation attack, which the current stored-counter design\n  happens to be immune to. Mitigate it the standard way: virtual shares/assets offsets as\n  in OpenZeppelin's ERC4626, or a dead-shares mint on the first deposit.\n- Round in the vault's favour: shares down on deposit, assets down on withdrawal (already\n  the case via `mulDiv` default), and shares *up* when burning for a given asset amount.\n\nThe cleanest path is to stop hand-rolling this and inherit `ERC4626` from OpenZeppelin,\noverriding `totalAssets()` to return the aUSDT balance and `_deposit`/`_withdraw` to route\nthrough Aave. That also gets you transferable share tokens and the inflation-attack\ndefences for free. If you keep the bespoke version, F-2, F-3 and F-6 all need fixing\nindividually.\n\n---\n\n<a name=\"f-3\"></a>\n## F-3 — High — the withdrawal fee is destroyed, not redistributed\n\n`README.md` and the contract's own NatSpec (`src/UsdtYieldVault.sol:17-18`) both state:\n\n> Both fees stay supplied in Aave and accrue to the remaining shareholders — they are not\n> swept to the owner.\n\nThat is true of the deposit fee. It is **false of the withdrawal fee**, which is charged to\nthe leaver and credited to nobody.\n\n`src/UsdtYieldVault.sol:111-119`:\n\n```solidity\nuint256 grossAssets = convertToAssets(shares);\nuint256 fee = (grossAssets * WITHDRAW_FEE_BPS) / BPS_DENOMINATOR;\nnetAssets = grossAssets - fee;\n...\ntotalAssetsStored -= grossAssets;      // <-- drops by the GROSS amount\naavePool.withdraw(address(usdt), netAssets, msg.sender);   // <-- only NET leaves Aave\n```\n\n`totalAssetsStored` falls by `grossAssets` but only `netAssets` is withdrawn. The fee stays\nin Aave *and* is deducted from the pool of assets the remaining shares can claim. Both\nsides of the ledger lose it. For the fee to accrue to remaining shareholders as documented,\n`totalAssetsStored` would have to drop by `netAssets`.\n\n### Evidence\n\nFrom the `test/audit/Accounting.t.sol` output above:\n\n```\n[FAIL: withdrawal fee was charged but credited to nobody: 1 !~= 30015007 (max delta: 1, real delta: 30015006)] test_WithdrawFeeAccruesToRemainingShareholders() (gas: 352699)\nLogs:\n  alice withdrawal fee charged : 30015007\n  bob claim before alice exited: 9994997498\n  bob claim after alice exited : 9994997499\n  bob actually gained          : 1\n```\n\nAlice pays a 30.015007 USDT exit fee. Bob is the only remaining shareholder, so the whole\nthing should land on him. He gains **1 base unit — 0.000001 USDT** — which is rounding\ndust, not the fee.\n\nAnd with no interest in play at all, purely from fees:\n\n```\n[FAIL: withdrawal fees are unrecoverable, not redistributed: 59999999 != 0] test_FeesAloneDoNotStrandValue() (gas: 372153)\nLogs:\n  totalShares                  : 0\n  aUSDT stranded in vault      : 59999999\n```\n\nTwo users deposit, both fully exit. Every share is burned. 60 USDT of fees remain in Aave\nunder the vault's address, claimable by nobody, forever.\n\n### Cross-check: stateful invariants\n\nRather than rely on hand-picked scenarios, `test/audit/Invariant.t.sol` fuzzes random\nsequences of deposits, withdrawals and interest accrual across four actors and asserts two\nproperties any custodial vault must hold.\n\n```\n$ forge test --match-path \"test/audit/Invariant.t.sol\"\n\n[PASS] invariant_VaultIsSolvent() (runs: 256, calls: 128000, reverts: 0)\n\n╭--------------+----------------+-------+---------+----------╮\n| Contract     | Selector       | Calls | Reverts | Discards |\n+============================================================+\n| VaultHandler | accrueInterest | 42410 | 0       | 0        |\n|--------------+----------------+-------+---------+----------|\n| VaultHandler | deposit        | 42754 | 0       | 0        |\n|--------------+----------------+-------+---------+----------|\n| VaultHandler | withdraw       | 42836 | 0       | 0        |\n╰--------------+----------------+-------+---------+----------╯\n\nSuite result: FAILED. 1 passed; 1 failed; 0 skipped; finished in 12.97s (12.97s CPU time)\n\nRan 1 test suite in 12.97s (12.97s CPU time): 1 tests passed, 1 failed, 0 skipped (2 total tests)\n\nFailing tests:\nEncountered 1 failing test in test/audit/Invariant.t.sol:VaultInvariantTest\n[FAIL: vault holds USDT that no share can ever claim: 32571445947 > 32436747203]\n\t[Sequence] (original: 6, shrunk: 2)\n\t\tsender=0x000000000000000000000000000000000000126c addr=[test/audit/Invariant.t.sol:VaultHandler]0x5991A2dF15A8F6A256D3Ec51E99254Cd3fb576A9 calldata=deposit(uint256,uint256) args=[146035894258372033511606425795166621410016652697163532950711606547201 [1.46e68], 58958160260005902355913856585609026662326974042294922880 [5.895e55]]\n\t\tsender=0x00000000000000000000000000000000000000fd addr=[test/audit/Invariant.t.sol:VaultHandler]0x5991A2dF15A8F6A256D3Ec51E99254Cd3fb576A9 calldata=withdraw(uint256,uint256) args=[1, 260241108242067510411887681004232935928026446966486646464580091742 [2.602e65]]\n invariant_AllVaultValueIsClaimable() (runs: 0, calls: 0, reverts: 0)\n```\n\nTwo results, and I want to be straight about both:\n\n- **`invariant_VaultIsSolvent` passes** across 128,000 calls. Shareholders can never claim\n  more than the vault owns. The vault is not insolvent — it is over-collateralised, which\n  is precisely the shape of F-2 and F-3. I am not claiming a solvency bug and you should\n  not read one here.\n- **`invariant_AllVaultValueIsClaimable` fails on a two-call sequence** — one deposit, one\n  withdrawal — leaving 134.7 USDT (`32571445947 - 32436747203`) that the contract owns and\n  no share can ever redeem.\n\nOne caveat on the solvency invariant, so you can judge it yourself: it tolerates 1 base\nunit of slack per deposit, because a rebasing aToken floors the scaled balance on mint.\nThat is a property of aTokens rather than of this vault, and the real chain confirms the\nmodel — in the fork log above, supplying exactly `100000000000` yields an aUSDT balance of\n`99999999999`. Without that tolerance the invariant fails by exactly 1 unit, which would be\nmy harness's rounding, not your bug.\n\n### Fix\n\nChange line 117 to deduct only what actually left the pool:\n\n```solidity\ntotalAssetsStored -= netAssets;\n```\n\nIf you adopt the F-2 fix and drive `totalAssets()` off the aUSDT balance, this line\ndisappears entirely and the behaviour becomes correct by construction: only `netAssets`\nleaves Aave, so the fee stays in the balance and lifts the share price for everyone left.\n\nEither way, decide explicitly what a lone depositor's fee should do. Today a sole\nshareholder pays a deposit fee to themselves (harmless but pointless), and a sole\nshareholder's *exit* fee is pure destruction. If fees are meant to be revenue, they need a\nrecipient and a collection function; if they are meant to reward stayers, they need to\nsurvive the last withdrawal.\n\n---\n\n<a name=\"f-4\"></a>\n## F-4 — Critical — the owner can front-run and confiscate a pending deposit\n\n`src/UsdtYieldVault.sol:126-130`:\n\n```solidity\nfunction setDepositFee(uint256 newFeeBps) external onlyOwner {\n    uint256 previousFeeBps = depositFeeBps;\n    depositFeeBps = newFeeBps;\n    emit DepositFeeUpdated(previousFeeBps, newFeeBps);\n}\n```\n\nNo upper bound, no timelock, effective in the same block. Combined with the documented\ndesign that the deposit fee \"accrues to the remaining shareholders\", this is a complete\ntheft primitive: the owner holds shares, sees a deposit in the mempool, raises the fee to\n99.99%, lets the victim's transaction land, and lowers it again. The victim's money is\ncredited to the owner's shares.\n\nThe owner never touches a transfer function, so nothing looks like a withdrawal. It reads\nas a fee adjustment.\n\n### Evidence\n\nUses the repo's own mocks — nothing here depends on my harness.\n\n```\n$ forge test --match-path \"test/audit/OwnerPowers.t.sol\" -vv\n\nRan 4 tests for test/audit/OwnerPowers.t.sol:OwnerPowersTest\n[FAIL: deposit fee can exceed 100%: 10001 > 10000] test_DepositFeeIsCapped() (gas: 24547)\nLogs:\n  depositFeeBps now            : 10001\n\n[FAIL: owner front-ran the deposit and took it: 10989010 < 9900000000] test_OwnerCannotConfiscateAPendingDeposit() (gas: 343384)\nLogs:\n  alice deposited              : 10000000000\n  alice can now claim          : 10989010\n  owner deposited              : 1000000000\n  owner can now claim          : 10989010989\n  value moved alice -> owner   : 9989010989\n\n[FAIL: EnforcedPause()] test_PauseCannotTrapExistingDeposits() (gas: 243890)\nLogs:\n  alice shares                 : 9990000000000000000000\n  alice claim (locked)         : 10000000000\n\n[PASS] test_Report_PausedPlusRenouncedIsTerminal() (gas: 210486)\nLogs:\n  owner                        : 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000\n  paused                       : true\n  USDT locked forever          : 10000000000\n\nSuite result: FAILED. 1 passed; 3 failed; 0 skipped; finished in 9.32ms (12.32ms CPU time)\n\nRan 1 test suite in 162.05ms (9.32ms CPU time): 1 tests passed, 3 failed, 0 skipped (4 total tests)\n```\n\nThe owner stakes 1,000 USDT. Alice deposits 10,000 USDT. After the sandwich, **Alice can\nclaim 10.98 USDT** and the owner can claim 10,989 USDT — **9,989 USDT moved from the\ndepositor to the owner in one block**, with an unchanged victim transaction.\n\n`test_DepositFeeIsCapped` shows the same setter accepts 10,001 bps — a fee above 100%,\nwhich makes `amount - fee` underflow and reverts every deposit until the owner relents.\n\n### Fix\n\n- Add a hard cap enforced in both the constructor and the setter, e.g.\n  `uint256 public constant MAX_DEPOSIT_FEE_BPS = 100;` with\n  `if (newFeeBps > MAX_DEPOSIT_FEE_BPS) revert FeeTooHigh();`. Cap it at a value you would\n  be willing to see applied to a deposit you did not expect.\n- Put `setDepositFee` behind a timelock so a change is announced before it can apply —\n  a two-step `queueFee` / `applyFee` with a delay of at least a few hours, or route\n  ownership through a `TimelockController`.\n- Give `deposit()` slippage protection: a `minSharesOut` parameter and\n  `if (shares < minSharesOut) revert Slippage();`. This is the defence that does not\n  depend on trusting the owner, and it costs one argument.\n- Hold ownership in a multisig, not an EOA.\n\n---\n\n<a name=\"f-5\"></a>\n## F-5 — High — `pause()` freezes withdrawal of money already deposited\n\n`withdraw()` carries `whenNotPaused` (`src/UsdtYieldVault.sol:107`). Pausing is a\nreasonable way to stop *new* deposits during an incident; applying it to withdrawals means\nthe owner key can trap depositor funds indefinitely. Users have no exit, no timeout, no\nemergency path.\n\n`Ownable` also exposes `renounceOwnership()`. Pausing and then renouncing puts the vault in\na state from which nobody — including the owner — can ever unpause it, because `unpause()`\nis `onlyOwner` and the owner is `address(0)`.\n\n### Evidence\n\nFrom the `test/audit/OwnerPowers.t.sol` output above:\n\n```\n[FAIL: EnforcedPause()] test_PauseCannotTrapExistingDeposits() (gas: 243890)\nLogs:\n  alice shares                 : 9990000000000000000000\n  alice claim (locked)         : 10000000000\n```\n\nAlice holds shares worth 10,000 USDT and cannot withdraw them.\n\nThe terminal state is reachable (this one passes — it documents the state rather than\nasserting against it):\n\n```\n[PASS] test_Report_PausedPlusRenouncedIsTerminal() (gas: 210486)\nLogs:\n  owner                        : 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000\n  paused                       : true\n  USDT locked forever          : 10000000000\n```\n\n### Fix\n\n- Drop `whenNotPaused` from `withdraw()`. Pausing deposits is the useful half; blocking\n  exits mostly converts an incident into a bank run you cannot serve later.\n- If you need to be able to halt withdrawals in a genuine emergency, make it a separate,\n  time-bounded flag — e.g. a `withdrawalsPausedUntil` timestamp capped at 72 hours — so it\n  cannot become permanent.\n- Override `renounceOwnership()` to revert. There is no scenario where this vault benefits\n  from having no owner.\n\n---\n\n<a name=\"f-6\"></a>\n## F-6 — Medium — dust withdrawals burn shares for zero USDT, and revert inside real Aave\n\n`convertToAssets` rounds down (`mulDiv`, default flooring). Since shares carry 18 decimals\nand USDT carries 6, any share amount below `totalShares / totalAssetsStored` converts to\nzero assets. `withdraw()` does not check for this: it burns the shares, computes a zero\nfee, subtracts zero from `totalAssetsStored`, and calls Aave for zero.\n\nTwo different bad outcomes depending on the pool:\n\n1. Against a permissive pool, the shares are silently destroyed for nothing.\n2. Against the **real** Aave V3 pool, `withdraw(asset, 0, to)` reverts with\n   `InvalidAmount()` — so a holder of a small position cannot exit at all.\n\n### Evidence\n\n```\n$ forge test --match-path \"test/audit/Rounding.t.sol\" -vv\n\nRan 3 tests for test/audit/Rounding.t.sol:RoundingTest\n[FAIL: shares burned for zero USDT: 0 <= 0; counterexample: calldata=0x27af79f300000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000715018a5 args=[1901074597 [1.901e9]]] testFuzz_WithdrawIsNeverAFreeBurn(uint256) (runs: 5, μ: 202833, ~: 202857)\n[FAIL: 26] test_DustWithdrawAgainstRealAaveSemantics() (gas: 1300192)\n[FAIL: shares burned for zero USDT: 0 <= 0] test_WithdrawNeverBurnsSharesForNothing() (gas: 257763)\nLogs:\n  shares burned                : 900000000000\n  USDT received                : 0\n  return value                 : 0\n\nSuite result: FAILED. 0 passed; 3 failed; 0 skipped; finished in 1.72ms (1.54ms CPU time)\n\nRan 1 test suite in 144.47ms (1.72ms CPU time): 0 tests passed, 3 failed, 0 skipped (3 total tests)\n```\n\n`test_WithdrawNeverBurnsSharesForNothing`: 900,000,000,000 shares burned, 0 USDT received.\nThe fuzzer finds the same class of input unaided.\n\n`[FAIL: 26]` is my `SafeAavePool` harness reproducing Aave's `INVALID_AMOUNT` guard. The\nreal pool confirms it — from the fork run in F-1:\n\n```\n[FAIL: custom error 0x2c5211c6] test_Fork_AaveAcceptsZeroWithdraw() (gas: 440252)\n```\n\n```\n$ cast 4byte 0x2c5211c6\nInvalidAmount()\n```\n\n### Fix\n\nRevert instead of burning for nothing, in `withdraw()` after computing `netAssets`:\n\n```solidity\nif (netAssets == 0) revert ZeroAssets();\n```\n\n`grossAssets == 0` would be the stricter check. Separately, consider rounding the burn in\nthe vault's favour and giving users a `redeem(assets)` entry point alongside\n`withdraw(shares)` so they are not forced to reason about an 18-decimal share unit for a\n6-decimal asset.\n\n---\n\n<a name=\"f-7\"></a>\n## F-7 — Medium — `deposit()` re-approves without zeroing first\n\nMainnet USDT's `approve` contains:\n\n```solidity\nrequire(!((_value != 0) && (allowed[msg.sender][_spender] != 0)));\n```\n\nAn existing non-zero allowance cannot be changed to another non-zero value; it must be set\nto zero first. `deposit()` calls `usdt.approve(address(aavePool), amount)` unconditionally\non every deposit.\n\nToday `supply()` consumes the full allowance so it returns to zero, which masks this. But\nany path that leaves a residual allowance — an Aave supply cap rejection after a partial\npull, a future pool implementation that does not consume the whole approval, a change in\nhow the vault batches supplies — leaves the vault permanently unable to deposit, with no\nadmin function to clear the allowance.\n\nThis is independent of F-1 and would survive a naive fix that only silences the return-value\nproblem (e.g. switching to a `IERC20NonStandard`-style interface without `forceApprove`).\n\n### Evidence\n\nAgainst real USDT on the fork — the second `approve` reverts:\n\n```\n[FAIL: raw approve failed] test_Fork_UsdtAllowsOverwritingNonZeroAllowance() (gas: 36918)\n```\n\nOffline, with the guard reproduced faithfully:\n\n```\n[FAIL: unsafe approve] test_ReApprovingANonZeroAllowanceSucceeds() (gas: 38373)\n```\n\n### Fix\n\n`SafeERC20.forceApprove` — the same one-line change recommended in F-1 — zeroes the\nallowance first and so fixes this too. This is why `forceApprove` is the right fix rather\nthan a bare low-level call that ignores the return value.\n\n---\n\n<a name=\"f-8\"></a>\n## F-8 — Low (latent) — USDT's transfer-fee switch would short-change the vault\n\nMainnet USDT has an owner-settable transfer fee (`basisPointsRate`, capped by\n`maximumFee`). Both read zero today:\n\n```\n$ cast call 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 \"basisPointsRate()(uint256)\" --rpc-url https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com\n0\n$ cast call 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 \"maximumFee()(uint256)\" --rpc-url https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com\n0\n$ cast call 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 \"owner()(address)\" --rpc-url https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com\n0xC6CDE7C39eB2f0F0095F41570af89eFC2C1Ea828\n```\n\nThe setter is live and callable by Tether. If it is ever turned on, `deposit()` breaks:\nline 93 pulls `amount` but the vault receives less, then line 95 supplies `amount` it does\nnot hold (revert), and lines 97-99 would have credited shares for the full `amount`.\n\nI am flagging this as latent, not active — it depends on a third party changing a\nparameter. It is on the list because the fix is cheap and the vault is named after this\nspecific token.\n\n### Evidence\n\nThis test passes; it demonstrates the mechanism and that the vault has no defence.\n\n```\n[PASS] test_Report_UsdtTransferFeeSwitchShortchangesTheVault() (gas: 121386)\nLogs:\n  amount passed to transfer    : 10000000000\n  amount actually received     : 9990000000\n  shortfall                    : 10000000\n```\n\n10 bps within Tether's own `setParams` limits costs the vault 10 USDT per 10,000\ntransferred.\n\n### Fix\n\nMeasure the delta rather than trusting the argument:\n\n```solidity\nuint256 balanceBefore = usdt.balanceOf(address(this));\nusdt.safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), amount);\nuint256 received = usdt.balanceOf(address(this)) - balanceBefore;\n```\n\nThen compute the fee, shares and the `supply()` amount from `received`, not `amount`. Apply\n`MIN_DEPOSIT` to `received` as well.\n\n---\n\n<a name=\"f-9\"></a>\n## F-9 — Low — constructor validation, dead state, event semantics\n\nThree smaller items, grouped:\n\n**No constructor validation.** `src/UsdtYieldVault.sol:72-79` accepts `_usdt`, `_aUsdt`,\n`_aavePool` and `_depositFeeBps` without checking any of them. A zero address or a\nmismatched aToken bricks the deployment silently, and `_depositFeeBps` bypasses whatever\ncap you add in F-4. *Fix:* revert on zero addresses, enforce the same fee cap as the\nsetter, and assert `IAToken(_aUsdt).UNDERLYING_ASSET_ADDRESS() == _usdt` — the real aUSDT\nexposes this, and I verified `0x23878914…D4086a` returns\n`0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7`.\n\n**`aUsdt` is written and never read** (see the grep in F-2). Today it is dead state that\ncosts a deploy-time slot and misleads readers into thinking the vault tracks its aToken\nposition. Under the F-2 fix it becomes load-bearing. Either use it or remove it.\n\n**Event semantics are inconsistent.** `Deposited` emits the *gross* `amount` alongside\n`fee` (line 101); `Withdrawn` emits the *net* `netAssets` alongside `fee` (line 121). Any\nindexer that treats the two symmetrically will mis-total. *Fix:* emit gross in both and let\nconsumers subtract, and document which it is in the NatSpec.\n\n---\n\n<a name=\"why-the-green-tick-was-empty\"></a>\n## Why the green tick was empty\n\nThe 39 tests do pass, and the coverage number is real:\n\n```\n$ forge coverage --match-path \"test/UsdtYieldVault.t.sol\" --no-match-coverage \"test/(mocks|harness)\"\n\nSuite result: ok. 39 passed; 0 failed; 0 skipped; finished in 4.95ms (20.71ms CPU time)\n\nRan 1 test suite in 150.80ms (4.95ms CPU time): 39 tests passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped (39 total tests)\n\n╭----------------------------+-----------------+----------------+---------------+-----------------╮\n| File                       | % Lines         | % Statements   | % Branches    | % Funcs         |\n+=================================================================================================+\n| src/UsdtYieldVault.sol     | 100.00% (52/52) | 98.25% (56/57) | 85.71% (6/7)  | 100.00% (11/11) |\n╰----------------------------+-----------------+----------------+---------------+-----------------╯\n```\n\nLine coverage measures whether a line *ran*. Every finding above is a line that ran and\nproduced the wrong answer. Specifically, the suite cannot detect:\n\n- **F-1, F-7, F-8** because `MockUSDT` is a stock OpenZeppelin ERC20. It returns `bool`\n  from `approve`, permits non-zero → non-zero allowance changes, and has no fee switch.\n  The vault has never been executed against anything resembling its own underlying asset.\n- **F-2** because `MockAavePool` mints a fixed-supply receipt token. There is no concept of\n  interest anywhere in the test suite, so a yield vault that pays no yield looks correct.\n  `test_DepositSuppliesToAave` asserts `aUsdt.balanceOf(vault) == DEPOSIT_AMOUNT` — an\n  assertion that can only hold in a world where Aave pays nothing.\n- **F-3** because no test has two users where one exits and the other's claim is checked\n  afterwards. `test_WithdrawReturnsUsdt` asserts `netAssets == 997e6`, confirming the fee\n  was *charged*, and nothing asserts where it went.\n- **F-4, F-5** because the owner tests only check that `onlyOwner` reverts for non-owners.\n  They test that the access control mechanism works, not what the owner can do with it.\n  `test_SetDepositFeeUpdatesValue` sets the fee to 25 bps and reads it back; nothing tries\n  10,001.\n- **F-6** because every withdrawal in the suite is `shares` or `shares / 2` of a round\n  1,000 USDT deposit, which never hits the rounding boundary.\n\nThe gap is not test count, it is assertion strength. The suite asserts that functions\nreturn the values the implementation happens to produce. It never asserts a property that\nthe implementation could violate — no invariant over multiple users, no conservation of\nvalue, no adversarial actor, and no contact with the two live contracts this thing is\nsupposed to talk to.\n\nFor what it is worth, the 15 failures I added come from 58 tests total:\n\n```\n$ forge test --no-match-path \"test/fork/*\"\n\nRan 6 test suites in 13.57s (27.17s CPU time): 43 tests passed, 15 failed, 0 skipped (58 total tests)\n```\n\n---\n\n## What I checked and did not find a problem with\n\nStated so you know where the review stopped, not as reassurance:\n\n- **Reentrancy.** Both state-changing functions carry `nonReentrant`, and neither USDT nor\n  aUSDT has transfer hooks. `withdraw()` updates all state before the external call\n  regardless. I found no reentrancy path.\n- **Solvency.** `invariant_VaultIsSolvent` held across 128,000 randomised calls. Shares\n  cannot claim more than the vault owns. The vault errs heavily in the *other* direction,\n  which is F-2 and F-3.\n- **Division by zero in `convertToShares`.** Reaching `totalAssetsStored == 0` while\n  `totalShares > 0` would brick deposits. It is not reachable: `grossAssets` rounds down,\n  so assets deplete strictly more slowly than shares. The invariant run did not produce it\n  either.\n- **First-depositor share inflation.** The usual donation attack does not work *as\n  currently written*, because `totalAssetsStored` is an internal counter that ignores\n  direct transfers. This immunity is an accident of the F-2 bug and **disappears the moment\n  you fix `totalAssets()`** — see the note in the F-2 fix.\n- **Access control.** `onlyOwner` is correctly applied to the three privileged functions.\n  The problem is the scope of those functions (F-4, F-5), not the modifier.\n- **Arithmetic.** Solidity 0.8.28 with `mulDiv` throughout; I found no overflow path other\n  than the intentional `amount - fee` underflow at fee > 100% noted in F-4.\n\nNot covered by this review: Aave-side risks the vault inherits and cannot control (reserve\nfreeze or pause blocking withdrawals, supply caps rejecting deposits, aUSDT liquidity\ncrunch), and any deployment or upgrade tooling, which I did not see.\n\n---\n\n## If it were my call\n\nThe two mechanical fixes — `forceApprove` (F-1, F-7) and `totalAssetsStored -= netAssets`\n(F-3) — are one-liners. F-2 is not: making `totalAssets()` balance-driven changes the share\nmaths and pulls in the inflation-attack defences the current design does not need. That is\nwhere I would spend the time, and it is the argument for inheriting OpenZeppelin's `ERC4626`\nrather than repairing the bespoke accounting.\n\nF-4 and F-5 are not bugs in the arithmetic; they are decisions about how much the owner key\nis trusted. Capping the fee, timelocking the setter, adding `minSharesOut`, and letting\nwithdrawals proceed while paused are each small, and together they change what a\ncompromised owner key can do from \"takes the deposits\" to \"stops new ones\".\n\nMonday is not enough time for F-2 plus a re-review of the share maths. I would move the\ndate.\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false}}

As the code stands, `deposit()` reverts on every call against\nthe real USDT at `0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7`, so the vault would go\nlive and immediately accept nothing. That failure is load-bearing for everything else:\nit means the contract has never been executed against its own underlying asset, and the\n39 green tests do not tell you otherwise.\n\nIf you fix only that one line, you ship a vault that pays depositors **0% yield**,\nstrands every dollar of Aave interest in a contract with no recovery function, and lets\nthe owner key take a pending deposit almost in full. Those are separate defects and each\none is demonstrated below.\n\nNothing under `src/` was modified. `test/UsdtYieldVault.t.sol` and `test/mocks/` are\nuntouched. All new code is in `test/audit/`, `test/harness/` and `test/fork/`.\n\n---\n\n## Contents\n\n| # | Severity | Finding |\n|---|---|---|\n| [F-1](#f-1) | Critical | `deposit()` always reverts against real USDT — the vault is inoperable on mainnet |\n| [F-2](#f-2) | Critical | Aave yield is never credited and is permanently unrecoverable; depositors end up poorer |\n| [F-3](#f-3) | High | The withdrawal fee is destroyed, not redistributed — contradicts the README |\n| [F-4](#f-4) | Critical | Owner can front-run and confiscate a pending deposit; deposit fee is uncapped |\n| [F-5](#f-5) | High | `pause()` freezes withdrawals of money already deposited; `renounceOwnership()` makes it permanent |\n| [F-6](#f-6) | Medium | Dust withdrawals burn shares for zero USDT locally, and revert inside real Aave |\n| [F-7](#f-7) | Medium | `deposit()` re-approves without zeroing; real USDT rejects non-zero → non-zero allowance changes |\n| [F-8](#f-8) | Low (latent) | USDT's transfer-fee switch would short-change the vault; no defence |\n| [F-9](#f-9) | Low | Constructor takes no validation; `aUsdt` is dead state; event semantics inconsistent |\n\nPlus [why the 39 tests and 100% coverage missed all of this](#why-the-green-tick-was-empty).\n\n---\n\n## How to reproduce\n\nEverything except `test/fork/` runs offline:\n\n```bash\nforge test --no-match-path \"test/fork/*\"\n```\n\nThe fork tests hit mainnet at a pinned block and need an archive endpoint. They default\nto `https://eth.drpc.org`, which served block 25,600,000 when I ran them; override with\nyour own if you prefer:\n\n```bash\nforge test --match-path \"test/fork/*\" -vv\n# or\nMAINNET_RPC_URL=https://your-endpoint forge test --match-path \"test/fork/*\" -vv\n```\n\n**Almost every test I added is written to fail.** Each one asserts a property the\ncontract is supposed to have, so the failure message *is* the evidence. A handful named\n`test_Report_*` / `test_Fork_Report_*` pass on purpose — those measure the size of a\nproblem rather than assert a property, and they are labelled as such below.\n\n### Files added\n\n| File | Purpose |\n|---|---|\n| `test/harness/NonStandardUsdt.sol` | Local USDT with mainnet TetherToken semantics (no return values, allowance guard, fee switch) |\n| `test/harness/AccruingAavePool.sol` | Aave pool stand-in whose aToken actually rebases, like real aUSDT |\n| `test/harness/SafeAavePool.sol` | Aave pool stand-in that moves tokens with SafeERC20 and rejects zero withdrawals, like real Aave |\n| `test/audit/RealUsdtCompat.t.sol` | F-1, F-7, F-8 offline |\n| `test/audit/Accounting.t.sol` | F-2, F-3 |\n| `test/audit/OwnerPowers.t.sol` | F-4, F-5 |\n| `test/audit/Rounding.t.sol` | F-6 |\n| `test/audit/Invariant.t.sol` | Stateful invariants quantifying F-2/F-3 |\n| `test/fork/MainnetUsdt.t.sol` | F-1, F-6, F-7 against the real mainnet contracts |\n\nThe three harness contracts exist because the repo's own mocks model neither of the two\nthings that matter: `MockUSDT` is a stock OpenZeppelin ERC20 (real USDT is not one), and\n`MockAavePool` mints a fixed-supply receipt token (real aUSDT rebases). I left both mocks\nin place as instructed and added new ones alongside.\n\n---\n\n<a name=\"f-1\"></a>\n## F-1 — Critical — `deposit()` always reverts against real USDT\n\n`src/UsdtYieldVault.sol:94`:\n\n```solidity\nusdt.approve(address(aavePool), amount);\n```\n\n`usdt` is typed `IERC20`, whose `approve` is declared `returns (bool)`. Solidity therefore\nemits an ABI decode of 32 bytes of return data after the call. Mainnet USDT (TetherToken)\ndeclares `function approve(address _spender, uint _value) public` — **no return value**.\nThe call itself succeeds and returns zero bytes; the decode then reverts.\n\nThe vault pulls the user's USDT on line 93 and dies on line 94. Every deposit, every user,\nevery time. line\n93 — line 94 is the one place it was skipped. Replace it with `forceApprove`, which\ntolerates missing return values *and* handles the zero-first requirement in F-7:\n\n```solidity\nusdt.forceApprove(address(aavePool), amount);\n```\n\n`using SafeERC20 for IERC20` is already declared on line 20, so this is a one-word change.\nSetting the allowance back to zero after `supply` returns (or approving `type(uint256).max`\nonce in the constructor) are both reasonable, but `forceApprove` per deposit is the\nsmallest correct change.\n\nDo not rely on `IERC20` for any other USDT call. `safeTransferFrom` on line 93 is already\ncorrect; there are no other direct token calls.\n\n---\n\n<a name=\"f-2\"></a>\n## F-2 — Critical — Aave yield is never credited, and is permanently unrecoverable\n\n`src/UsdtYieldVault.sol:143-145`:\n\n```solidity\nfunction totalAssets() public view returns (uint256) {\n    return totalAssetsStored;\n}\n```\n\n`totalAssetsStored` is a plain counter: it goes up by `amount` in `deposit()` and down by\n`grossAssets` in `withdraw()`. Nothing else writes it. Meanwhile the vault's actual\nposition is `aUsdt.balanceOf(address(this))`, which rebases upward continuously — that is\nthe entire reason for supplying to Aave.\n\nSince every share price calculation (`convertToShares`, `convertToAssets`,\n`balanceOfUnderlying`, `sharePrice`) is driven by `totalAssetsStored`, **no depositor can\never withdraw a cent of interest.** It accumulates as aUSDT owned by the vault.\n\nThere is no way to get it out. The only outbound call in the whole contract is:\n\n```\n$ grep -nE \"safeTransfer|\\.transfer\\(|withdraw\\(|sweep|rescue|skim\" src/UsdtYieldVault.sol\n93:        usdt.safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), amount);\n107:    function withdraw(uint256 shares) external whenNotPaused nonReentrant returns (uint256 netAssets) {\n119:        aavePool.withdraw(address(usdt), netAssets, msg.sender);\n```\n\nLine 119 is share-driven, and shares can only ever claim `totalAssetsStored`. There is no\nsweep, no rescue, no fee collector. The interest is gone.\n\nThe `aUsdt` immutable — the one piece of state that would fix this — is stored and never\nread:\n\n```\n$ grep -n \"aUsdt\" src/UsdtYieldVault.sol\n41:    IERC20 public immutable aUsdt;\n68:    /// @param _aUsdt The Aave aUSDT receipt token.\n72:    constructor(address _usdt, address _aUsdt, address _aavePool, uint256 _depositFeeBps, address initialOwner)\n76:        aUsdt = IERC20(_aUsdt);\n```\n\n### Evidence\n\n`test/harness/AccruingAavePool.sol` is an Aave stand-in whose aToken rebases the way real\naUSDT does (scaled balance × liquidity index). `pool.accrue(500)` pays 5% interest and\nbacks it with real underlying, exactly as Aave does.\n\n```\n$ forge test --match-path \"test/audit/Accounting.t.sol\" -vv\n\nRan 6 tests for test/audit/Accounting.t.sol:AccountingTest\n[FAIL: withdrawal fees are unrecoverable, not redistributed: 59999999 != 0] test_FeesAloneDoNotStrandValue() (gas: 372153)\nLogs:\n  totalShares the position earning 5%: 999970000000 < 1000000000000] test_SoleDepositorEarnsTheYield() (gas: 276400)\nLogs:\n  alice deposited              : 10000000000\n  alice got back after +5% APY : 9970000000\n  wallet before                : 1000000000000\n  wallet after                 : 999970000000\n\n[FAIL: totalAssets() ignores accrued Aave interest: 10000000000 != 10500000000] Alice deposits 10,000 USDT. The position\nearns 5%. She withdraws everything and gets back **9,970 USDT**. She is 30 USDT poorer\nthan if she had done nothing at all, while 530 USDT of her money sits in Aave under the\nvault's address with no function that can move it.\n\n`test_Report_LeakOverOneYear` (passes, it is a measurement) puts a number on it: after one\nyear at ~5% on a 20,000 USDT deposit, **479 bps of TVL — 1,006 USDT — is unclaimable.**\nThat is the yield the product is named after.\n\nThe rate is not hypothetical. On the real Aave pool at the pinned block, USDT was paying\n276 bps and the aUSDT balance really does rebase — from the fork run in F-1:\n\n```\n  supplied to real Aave        : 100000000000\n  aUSDT after supply           : 99999999999\n  aUSDT after 365 days         : 102765734567\n  interest earned              : 2765734568\n  implied APY, bps             : 276\n```\n\n### Fix\n\nMake `totalAssets()` read the position instead of a stored counter:\n\n```solidity\nfunction totalAssets() public view returns (uint256) {\n    return aUsdt.balanceOf(address(this));\n}\n```\n\nThen delete `totalAssetsStored` and every write to it, and change `convertToShares` /\n`convertToAssets` / `sharePrice` to call `totalAssets()`. Note that `convertToShares` must\nread the balance *before* the new deposit is supplied, so keep the share calculation ahead\nof the `supply()` call as it is today.\n\nTwo things to get right while you are in there:\n\n- With a balance-driven `totalAssets()`, the vault becomes vulnerable to the classic\n  first-depositor donation/inflation attack, which the current stored-counter design\n  happens to be immune to. Mitigate it the standard way: virtual shares/assets offsets as\n  in OpenZeppelin's ERC4626, or a dead-shares mint on the first deposit.\n- Round in the vault's favour: shares down on deposit, assets down on withdrawal (already\n  the case via `mulDiv` default), and shares *up* when burning for a given asset amount.\n\nThe cleanest path is to stop hand-rolling this and inherit `ERC4626` from OpenZeppelin,\noverriding `totalAssets()` to return the aUSDT balance and `_deposit`/`_withdraw` to route\nthrough Aave. That also gets you transferable share tokens and the inflation-attack\ndefences for free. If you keep the bespoke version, F-2, F-3 and F-6 all need fixing\nindividually.\n\n---\n\n<a name=\"f-3\"></a>\n## F-3 — High — the withdrawal fee is destroyed, not redistributed\n\n`README.md` and the contract's own NatSpec (`src/UsdtYieldVault.sol:17-18`) both state:\n\n> Both fees stay supplied in Aave and accrue to the remaining shareholders — they are not\n> swept to the owner.\n\nThat is true of the deposit fee. It is **false of the withdrawal fee**, which is charged to\nthe leaver and credited to nobody.\n\n`src/UsdtYieldVault.sol:111-119`:\n\n```solidity\nuint256 grossAssets = convertToAssets(shares);\nuint256 fee = (grossAssets * WITHDRAW_FEE_BPS) / BPS_DENOMINATOR;\nnetAssets = grossAssets - fee;\n...\ntotalAssetsStored -= grossAssets;      // <-- drops by the GROSS amount\naavePool.withdraw(address(usdt), netAssets, msg.sender);   // <-- only NET leaves Aave\n```\n\n`totalAssetsStored` falls by `grossAssets` but only `netAssets` is withdrawn. The fee stays\nin Aave *and* is deducted from the pool of assets the remaining shares can claim. Both\nsides of the ledger lose it. For the fee to accrue to remaining shareholders as documented,\n`totalAssetsStored` would have to drop by `netAssets`.\n\n### Evidence\n\nFrom the `test/audit/Accounting.t.sol` output above:\n\n```\n[FAIL: withdrawal fee was charged but credited to nobody: 1 !~= 30015007 (max delta: 1, real delta: 30015006)] test_WithdrawFeeAccruesToRemainingShareholders() (gas: 352699)\nLogs:\n  alice withdrawal fee charged : 30015007\n  bob claim before alice exited: 9994997498\n  bob claim after alice exited : 9994997499\n  bob actually gained          : 1\n```\n\nAlice pays a 30.015007 USDT exit fee. Bob is the only remaining shareholder, so the whole\nthing should land on him. He gains **1 base unit — 0.000001 USDT** — which is rounding\ndust, not the fee.\n\nAnd with no interest in play at all, purely from fees:\n\n```\n[FAIL: withdrawal fees are unrecoverable, not redistributed: 59999999 != 0] test_FeesAloneDoNotStrandValue() (gas: 372153)\nLogs:\n  totalShares                  : 0\n  aUSDT stranded in vault      : 59999999\n```\n\nTwo users deposit, both fully exit. Every share is burned. 60 USDT of fees remain in Aave\nunder the vault's address, claimable by nobody, forever.\n\n### Cross-check: stateful invariants\n\nRather than rely on hand-picked scenarios, `test/audit/Invariant.t.sol` fuzzes random\nsequences of deposits, withdrawals and interest accrual across four actors and asserts two\nproperties any custodial vault must hold.\n\n```\n$ forge test --match-path \"test/audit/Invariant.t.sol\"\n\n[PASS] invariant_VaultIsSolvent() (runs: 256, calls: 128000, reverts: 0)\n\n╭--------------+----------------+-------+---------+----------╮\n| Contract     | Selector       | Calls | Reverts | Discards |\n+============================================================+\n| VaultHandler | accrueInterest | 42410 | 0       | 0        |\n|--------------+----------------+-------+---------+----------|\n| VaultHandler | deposit        | 42754 | 0       | 0        |\n|--------------+----------------+-------+---------+----------|\n| VaultHandler | withdraw       | 42836 | 0       | 0        |\n╰--------------+----------------+-------+---------+----------╯\n\nSuite result: FAILED. 1 passed; 1 failed; 0 skipped; finished in 12.97s (12.97s CPU time)\n\nRan 1 test suite in 12.97s (12.97s CPU time): 1 tests passed, 1 failed, 0 skipped (2 total tests)\n\nFailing tests:\nEncountered 1 failing test in test/audit/Invariant.t.sol:VaultInvariantTest\n[FAIL: vault holds USDT that no share can ever claim: 32571445947 > 32436747203]\n\t[Sequence] (original: 6, shrunk: 2)\n\t\tsender=0x000000000000000000000000000000000000126c addr=[test/audit/Invariant.t.sol:VaultHandler]0x5991A2dF15A8F6A256D3Ec51E99254Cd3fb576A9 calldata=deposit(uint256,uint256) args=[146035894258372033511606425795166621410016652697163532950711606547201 [1.46e68], 58958160260005902355913856585609026662326974042294922880 [5.895e55]]\n\t\tsender=0x00000000000000000000000000000000000000fd addr=[test/audit/Invariant.t.sol:VaultHandler]0x5991A2dF15A8F6A256D3Ec51E99254Cd3fb576A9 calldata=withdraw(uint256,uint256) args=[1, 260241108242067510411887681004232935928026446966486646464580091742 [2.602e65]]\n invariant_AllVaultValueIsClaimable() (runs: 0, calls: 0, reverts: 0)\n```\n\nTwo results, and I want to be straight about both:\n\n- **`invariant_VaultIsSolvent` passes** across 128,000 calls. Shareholders can never claim\n  more than the vault owns. The vault is not insolvent — it is over-collateralised, which\n  is precisely the shape of F-2 and F-3. I am not claiming a solvency bug and you should\n  not read one here.\n- **`invariant_AllVaultValueIsClaimable` fails on a two-call sequence** — one deposit, one\n  withdrawal — leaving 134.7 USDT (`32571445947 - 32436747203`) that the contract owns and\n  no share can ever redeem.\n\nOne caveat on the solvency invariant, so you can judge it yourself: it tolerates 1 base\nunit of slack per deposit, because a rebasing aToken floors the scaled balance on mint.\nThat is a property of aTokens rather than of this vault, and the real chain confirms the\nmodel — in the fork log above, supplying exactly `100000000000` yields an aUSDT balance of\n`99999999999`. Without that tolerance the invariant fails by exactly 1 unit, which would be\nmy harness's rounding, not your bug.\n\n### Fix\n\nChange line 117 to deduct only what actually left the pool:\n\n```solidity\ntotalAssetsStored -= netAssets;\n```\n\nIf you adopt the F-2 fix and drive `totalAssets()` off the aUSDT balance, this line\ndisappears entirely and the behaviour becomes correct by construction: only `netAssets`\nleaves Aave, so the fee stays in the balance and lifts the share price for everyone left.\n\nEither way, decide explicitly what a lone depositor's fee should do. Today a sole\nshareholder pays a deposit fee to themselves (harmless but pointless), and a sole\nshareholder's *exit* fee is pure destruction. If fees are meant to be revenue, they need a\nrecipient and a collection function; if they are meant to reward stayers, they need to\nsurvive the last withdrawal.\n\n---\n\n<a name=\"f-4\"></a>\n## F-4 — Critical — the owner can front-run and confiscate a pending deposit\n\n`src/UsdtYieldVault.sol:126-130`:\n\n```solidity\nfunction setDepositFee(uint256 newFeeBps) external onlyOwner {\n    uint256 previousFeeBps = depositFeeBps;\n    depositFeeBps = newFeeBps;\n    emit DepositFeeUpdated(previousFeeBps, newFeeBps);\n}\n```\n\nNo upper bound, no timelock, effective in the same block. Combined with the documented\ndesign that the deposit fee \"accrues to the remaining shareholders\", this is a complete\ntheft primitive: the owner holds shares, sees a deposit in the mempool, raises the fee to\n99.99%, lets the victim's transaction land, and lowers it again. The victim's money is\ncredited to the owner's shares.\n\nThe owner never touches a transfer function, so nothing looks like a withdrawal. It reads\nas a fee adjustment.\n\n### Evidence\n\nUses the repo's own mocks — nothing here depends on my harness.\n\n```\n$ forge test --match-path \"test/audit/OwnerPowers.t.sol\" -vv\n\nRan 4 tests for test/audit/OwnerPowers.t.sol:OwnerPowersTest\n[FAIL: deposit fee can exceed 100%: 10001 > 10000] test_DepositFeeIsCapped() (gas: 24547)\nLogs:\n  depositFeeBps now            : 10001\n\n[FAIL: owner front-ran the deposit and took it: 10989010 < 9900000000] test_OwnerCannotConfiscateAPendingDeposit() (gas: 343384)\nLogs:\n  alice deposited              : 10000000000\n  alice can now claim          : 10989010\n  owner deposited              : 1000000000\n  owner can now claim          : 10989010989\n  value moved alice -> owner   : 9989010989\n\n[FAIL: EnforcedPause()] test_PauseCannotTrapExistingDeposits() (gas: 243890)\nLogs:\n  alice shares                 : 9990000000000000000000\n  alice claim (locked)         : 10000000000\n\n[PASS] test_Report_PausedPlusRenouncedIsTerminal() (gas: 210486)\nLogs:\n  owner                        : 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000\n  paused                       : true\n  USDT locked forever          : 10000000000\n\nSuite result: FAILED. 1 passed; 3 failed; 0 skipped; finished in 9.32ms (12.32ms CPU time)\n\nRan 1 test suite in 162.05ms (9.32ms CPU time): 1 tests passed, 3 failed, 0 skipped (4 total tests)\n```\n\nThe owner stakes 1,000 USDT. Alice deposits 10,000 USDT. After the sandwich, **Alice can\nclaim 10.98 USDT** and the owner can claim 10,989 USDT — **9,989 USDT moved from the\ndepositor to the owner in one block**, with an unchanged victim transaction.\n\n`test_DepositFeeIsCapped` shows the same setter accepts 10,001 bps — a fee above 100%,\nwhich makes `amount - fee` underflow and reverts every deposit until the owner relents.\n\n### Fix\n\n- Add a hard cap enforced in both the constructor and the setter, e.g.\n  `uint256 public constant MAX_DEPOSIT_FEE_BPS = 100;` with\n  `if (newFeeBps > MAX_DEPOSIT_FEE_BPS) revert FeeTooHigh();`. Cap it at a value you would\n  be willing to see applied to a deposit you did not expect.\n- Put `setDepositFee` behind a timelock so a change is announced before it can apply —\n  a two-step `queueFee` / `applyFee` with a delay of at least a few hours, or route\n  ownership through a `TimelockController`.\n- Give `deposit()` slippage protection: a `minSharesOut` parameter and\n  `if (shares < minSharesOut) revert Slippage();`. This is the defence that does not\n  depend on trusting the owner, and it costs one argument.\n- Hold ownership in a multisig, not an EOA.\n\n---\n\n<a name=\"f-5\"></a>\n## F-5 — High — `pause()` freezes withdrawal of money already deposited\n\n`withdraw()` carries `whenNotPaused` (`src/UsdtYieldVault.sol:107`). Pausing is a\nreasonable way to stop *new* deposits during an incident; applying it to withdrawals means\nthe owner key can trap depositor funds indefinitely. Users have no exit, no timeout, no\nemergency path.\n\n`Ownable` also exposes `renounceOwnership()`. Pausing and then renouncing puts the vault in\na state from which nobody — including the owner — can ever unpause it, because `unpause()`\nis `onlyOwner` and the owner is `address(0)`.\n\n### Evidence\n\nFrom the `test/audit/OwnerPowers.t.sol` output above:\n\n```\n[FAIL: EnforcedPause()] test_PauseCannotTrapExistingDeposits() (gas: 243890)\nLogs:\n  alice shares                 : 9990000000000000000000\n  alice claim (locked)         : 10000000000\n```\n\nAlice holds shares worth 10,000 USDT and cannot withdraw them.\n\nThe terminal state is reachable (this one passes — it documents the state rather than\nasserting against it):\n\n```\n[PASS] test_Report_PausedPlusRenouncedIsTerminal() (gas: 210486)\nLogs:\n  owner                        : 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000\n  paused                       : true\n  USDT locked forever          : 10000000000\n```\n\n### Fix\n\n- Drop `whenNotPaused` from `withdraw()`. Pausing deposits is the useful half; blocking\n  exits mostly converts an incident into a bank run you cannot serve later.\n- If you need to be able to halt withdrawals in a genuine emergency, make it a separate,\n  time-bounded flag — e.g. a `withdrawalsPausedUntil` timestamp capped at 72 hours — so it\n  cannot become permanent.\n- Override `renounceOwnership()` to revert. There is no scenario where this vault benefits\n  from having no owner.\n\n---\n\n<a name=\"f-6\"></a>\n## F-6 — Medium — dust withdrawals burn shares for zero USDT, and revert inside real Aave\n\n`convertToAssets` rounds down (`mulDiv`, default flooring). Since shares carry 18 decimals\nand USDT carries 6, any share amount below `totalShares / totalAssetsStored` converts to\nzero assets. `withdraw()` does not check for this: it burns the shares, computes a zero\nfee, subtracts zero from `totalAssetsStored`, and calls Aave for zero.\n\nTwo different bad outcomes depending on the pool:\n\n1. Against a permissive pool, the shares are silently destroyed for nothing.\n2. Against the **real** Aave V3 pool, `withdraw(asset, 0, to)` reverts with\n   `InvalidAmount()` — so a holder of a small position cannot exit at all.\n\n### Evidence\n\n```\n$ forge test --match-path \"test/audit/Rounding.t.sol\" -vv\n\nRan 3 tests for test/audit/Rounding.t.sol:RoundingTest\n[FAIL: shares burned for zero USDT: 0 <= 0; counterexample: calldata=0x27af79f300000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000715018a5 args=[1901074597 [1.901e9]]] testFuzz_WithdrawIsNeverAFreeBurn(uint256) (runs: 5, μ: 202833, ~: 202857)\n[FAIL: 26] test_DustWithdrawAgainstRealAaveSemantics() (gas: 1300192)\n[FAIL: shares burned for zero USDT: 0 <= 0] test_WithdrawNeverBurnsSharesForNothing() (gas: 257763)\nLogs:\n  shares burned                : 900000000000\n  USDT received                : 0\n  return value                 : 0\n\nSuite result: FAILED. 0 passed; 3 failed; 0 skipped; finished in 1.72ms (1.54ms CPU time)\n\nRan 1 test suite in 144.47ms (1.72ms CPU time): 0 tests passed, 3 failed, 0 skipped (3 total tests)\n```\n\n`test_WithdrawNeverBurnsSharesForNothing`: 900,000,000,000 shares burned, 0 USDT received.\nThe fuzzer finds the same class of input unaided.\n\n`[FAIL: 26]` is my `SafeAavePool` harness reproducing Aave's `INVALID_AMOUNT` guard. The\nreal pool confirms it — from the fork run in F-1:\n\n```\n[FAIL: custom error 0x2c5211c6] test_Fork_AaveAcceptsZeroWithdraw() (gas: 440252)\n```\n\n```\n$ cast 4byte 0x2c5211c6\nInvalidAmount()\n```\n\n### Fix\n\nRevert instead of burning for nothing, in `withdraw()` after computing `netAssets`:\n\n```solidity\nif (netAssets == 0) revert ZeroAssets();\n```\n\n`grossAssets == 0` would be the stricter check. Separately, consider rounding the burn in\nthe vault's favour and giving users a `redeem(assets)` entry point alongside\n`withdraw(shares)` so they are not forced to reason about an 18-decimal share unit for a\n6-decimal asset.\n\n---\n\n<a name=\"f-7\"></a>\n## F-7 — Medium — `deposit()` re-approves without zeroing first\n\nMainnet USDT's `approve` contains:\n\n```solidity\nrequire(!((_value != 0) && (allowed[msg.sender][_spender] != 0)));\n```\n\nAn existing non-zero allowance cannot be changed to another non-zero value; it must be set\nto zero first. `deposit()` calls `usdt.approve(address(aavePool), amount)` unconditionally\non every deposit.\n\nToday `supply()` consumes the full allowance so it returns to zero, which masks this. But\nany path that leaves a residual allowance — an Aave supply cap rejection after a partial\npull, a future pool implementation that does not consume the whole approval, a change in\nhow the vault batches supplies — leaves the vault permanently unable to deposit, with no\nadmin function to clear the allowance.\n\nThis is independent of F-1 and would survive a naive fix that only silences the return-value\nproblem (e.g. switching to a `IERC20NonStandard`-style interface without `forceApprove`).\n\n### Evidence\n\nAgainst real USDT on the fork — the second `approve` reverts:\n\n```\n[FAIL: raw approve failed] test_Fork_UsdtAllowsOverwritingNonZeroAllowance() (gas: 36918)\n```\n\nOffline, with the guard reproduced faithfully:\n\n```\n[FAIL: unsafe approve] test_ReApprovingANonZeroAllowanceSucceeds() (gas: 38373)\n```\n\n### Fix\n\n`SafeERC20.forceApprove` — the same one-line change recommended in F-1 — zeroes the\nallowance first and so fixes this too. This is why `forceApprove` is the right fix rather\nthan a bare low-level call that ignores the return value.\n\n---\n\n<a name=\"f-8\"></a>\n## F-8 — Low (latent) — USDT's transfer-fee switch would short-change the vault\n\nMainnet USDT has an owner-settable transfer fee (`basisPointsRate`, capped by\n`maximumFee`). Both read zero today:\n\n```\n$ cast call 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 \"basisPointsRate()(uint256)\" --rpc-url https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com\n0\n$ cast call 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 \"maximumFee()(uint256)\" --rpc-url https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com\n0\n$ cast call 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 \"owner()(address)\" --rpc-url https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com\n0xC6CDE7C39eB2f0F0095F41570af89eFC2C1Ea828\n```\n\nThe setter is live and callable by Tether. If it is ever turned on, `deposit()` breaks:\nline 93 pulls `amount` but the vault receives less, then line 95 supplies `amount` it does\nnot hold (revert), and lines 97-99 would have credited shares for the full `amount`.\n\nI am flagging this as latent, not active — it depends on a third party changing a\nparameter. It is on the list because the fix is cheap and the vault is named after this\nspecific token.\n\n### Evidence\n\nThis test passes; it demonstrates the mechanism and that the vault has no defence.\n\n```\n[PASS] test_Report_UsdtTransferFeeSwitchShortchangesTheVault() (gas: 121386)\nLogs:\n  amount passed to transfer    : 10000000000\n  amount actually received     : 9990000000\n  shortfall                    : 10000000\n```\n\n10 bps within Tether's own `setParams` limits costs the vault 10 USDT per 10,000\ntransferred.\n\n### Fix\n\nMeasure the delta rather than trusting the argument:\n\n```solidity\nuint256 balanceBefore = usdt.balanceOf(address(this));\nusdt.safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), amount);\nuint256 received = usdt.balanceOf(address(this)) - balanceBefore;\n```\n\nThen compute the fee, shares and the `supply()` amount from `received`, not `amount`. Apply\n`MIN_DEPOSIT` to `received` as well.\n\n---\n\n<a name=\"f-9\"></a>\n## F-9 — Low — constructor validation, dead state, event semantics\n\nThree smaller items, grouped:\n\n**No constructor validation.** `src/UsdtYieldVault.sol:72-79` accepts `_usdt`, `_aUsdt`,\n`_aavePool` and `_depositFeeBps` without checking any of them. A zero address or a\nmismatched aToken bricks the deployment silently, and `_depositFeeBps` bypasses whatever\ncap you add in F-4. *Fix:* revert on zero addresses, enforce the same fee cap as the\nsetter, and assert `IAToken(_aUsdt).UNDERLYING_ASSET_ADDRESS() == _usdt` — the real aUSDT\nexposes this, and I verified `0x23878914…D4086a` returns\n`0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7`.\n\n**`aUsdt` is written and never read** (see the grep in F-2). Today it is dead state that\ncosts a deploy-time slot and misleads readers into thinking the vault tracks its aToken\nposition. Under the F-2 fix it becomes load-bearing. Either use it or remove it.\n\n**Event semantics are inconsistent.** `Deposited` emits the *gross* `amount` alongside\n`fee` (line 101); `Withdrawn` emits the *net* `netAssets` alongside `fee` (line 121). Any\nindexer that treats the two symmetrically will mis-total. *Fix:* emit gross in both and let\nconsumers subtract, and document which it is in the NatSpec.\n\n---\n\n<a name=\"why-the-green-tick-was-empty\"></a>\n## Why the green tick was empty\n\nThe 39 tests do pass, and the coverage number is real:\n\n```\n$ forge coverage --match-path \"test/UsdtYieldVault.t.sol\" --no-match-coverage \"test/(mocks|harness)\"\n\nSuite result: ok. 39 passed; 0 failed; 0 skipped; finished in 4.95ms (20.71ms CPU time)\n\nRan 1 test suite in 150.80ms (4.95ms CPU time): 39 tests passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped (39 total tests)\n\n╭----------------------------+-----------------+----------------+---------------+-----------------╮\n| File                       | % Lines         | % Statements   | % Branches    | % Funcs         |\n+=================================================================================================+\n| src/UsdtYieldVault.sol     | 100.00% (52/52) | 98.25% (56/57) | 85.71% (6/7)  | 100.00% (11/11) |\n╰----------------------------+-----------------+----------------+---------------+-----------------╯\n```\n\nLine coverage measures whether a line *ran*. Every finding above is a line that ran and\nproduced the wrong answer. Specifically, the suite cannot detect:\n\n- **F-1, F-7, F-8** because `MockUSDT` is a stock OpenZeppelin ERC20. It returns `bool`\n  from `approve`, permits non-zero → non-zero allowance changes, and has no fee switch.\n  The vault has never been executed against anything resembling its own underlying asset.\n- **F-2** because `MockAavePool` mints a fixed-supply receipt token. There is no concept of\n  interest anywhere in the test suite, so a yield vault that pays no yield looks correct.\n  `test_DepositSuppliesToAave` asserts `aUsdt.balanceOf(vault) == DEPOSIT_AMOUNT` — an\n  assertion that can only hold in a world where Aave pays nothing.\n- **F-3** because no test has two users where one exits and the other's claim is checked\n  afterwards. `test_WithdrawReturnsUsdt` asserts `netAssets == 997e6`, confirming the fee\n  was *charged*, and nothing asserts where it went.\n- **F-4, F-5** because the owner tests only check that `onlyOwner` reverts for non-owners.\n  They test that the access control mechanism works, not what the owner can do with it.\n  `test_SetDepositFeeUpdatesValue` sets the fee to 25 bps and reads it back; nothing tries\n  10,001.\n- **F-6** because every withdrawal in the suite is `shares` or `shares / 2` of a round\n  1,000 USDT deposit, which never hits the rounding boundary.\n\nThe gap is not test count, it is assertion strength. The suite asserts that functions\nreturn the values the implementation happens to produce. It never asserts a property that\nthe implementation could violate — no invariant over multiple users, no conservation of\nvalue, no adversarial actor, and no contact with the two live contracts this thing is\nsupposed to talk to.\n\nFor what it is worth, the 15 failures I added come from 58 tests total:\n\n```\n$ forge test --no-match-path \"test/fork/*\"\n\nRan 6 test suites in 13.57s (27.17s CPU time): 43 tests passed, 15 failed, 0 skipped (58 total tests)\n```\n\n---\n\n## What I checked and did not find a problem with\n\nStated so you know where the review stopped, not as reassurance:\n\n- **Reentrancy.** Both state-changing functions carry `nonReentrant`, and neither USDT nor\n  aUSDT has transfer hooks. `withdraw()` updates all state before the external call\n  regardless. I found no reentrancy path.\n- **Solvency.** `invariant_VaultIsSolvent` held across 128,000 randomised calls. Shares\n  cannot claim more than the vault owns. The vault errs heavily in the *other* direction,\n  which is F-2 and F-3.\n- **Division by zero in `convertToShares`.** Reaching `totalAssetsStored == 0` while\n  `totalShares > 0` would brick deposits. It is not reachable: `grossAssets` rounds down,\n  so assets deplete strictly more slowly than shares. The invariant run did not produce it\n  either.\n- **First-depositor share inflation.** The usual donation attack does not work *as\n  currently written*, because `totalAssetsStored` is an internal counter that ignores\n  direct transfers. This immunity is an accident of the F-2 bug and **disappears the moment\n  you fix `totalAssets()`** — see the note in the F-2 fix.\n- **Access control.** `onlyOwner` is correctly applied to the three privileged functions.\n  The problem is the scope of those functions (F-4, F-5), not the modifier.\n- **Arithmetic.** Solidity 0.8.28 with `mulDiv` throughout; I found no overflow path other\n  than the intentional `amount - fee` underflow at fee > 100% noted in F-4.\n\nNot covered by this review: Aave-side risks the vault inherits and cannot control (reserve\nfreeze or pause blocking withdrawals, supply caps rejecting deposits, aUSDT liquidity\ncrunch), and any deployment or upgrade tooling, which I did not see.\n\n---\n\n## If it were my call\n\nThe two mechanical fixes — `forceApprove` (F-1, F-7) and `totalAssetsStored -= netAssets`\n(F-3) — are one-liners. F-2 is not: making `totalAssets()` balance-driven changes the share\nmaths and pulls in the inflation-attack defences the current design does not need. That is\nwhere I would spend the time, and it is the argument for inheriting OpenZeppelin's `ERC4626`\nrather than repairing the bespoke accounting.\n\nF-4 and F-5 are not bugs in the arithmetic; they are decisions about how much the owner key\nis trusted. Capping the fee, timelocking the setter, adding `minSharesOut`, and letting\nwithdrawals proceed while paused are each small, and together they change what a\ncompromised owner key can do from \"takes the deposits\" to \"stops new ones\".\n\nMonday is not enough time for F-2 plus a re-review of the share maths. I would move the\ndate.\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":59,"oldLines":6,"newStart":59,"newLines":37,"lines":[" `test_Report_*` / `test_Fork_Report_*` pass on purpose — those measure the size of a"," problem rather than assert a property, and they are labelled as such below."," ","+### Two things about re-running, so you do not chase a false mismatch","+","+**The randomised tests will not print my exact numbers.** `testFuzz_WithdrawIsNeverAFreeBurn`","+(F-6) and `invariant_AllVaultValueIsClaimable` (F-3) are seed-dependent: the failure","+reproduces every time, but the specific counterexample and the specific USDT amounts differ","+per run. I ran the invariant from a cold cache twice to check it is not luck — it failed","+both times, always shrinking to a 2-call sequence, while `invariant_VaultIsSolvent` passed","+both times at 128,000 calls:","+","+```","+=== COLD RUN 1: invariant ===","+[FAIL: vault holds USDT that no share can ever claim: 69043495022 > 68741034476]","+  [Sequence] (original: 4, shrunk: 2)","+[PASS] invariant_VaultIsSolvent() (runs: 256, calls: 128000, reverts: 0)","+Suite result: FAILED. 1 passed; 1 failed; 0 skipped; finished in 13.52s (13.52s CPU time)","+=== COLD RUN 2: invariant ===","+[FAIL: vault holds USDT that no share can ever claim: 51914023818 > 51763908489]","+  [Sequence] (original: 4, shrunk: 2)","+[PASS] invariant_VaultIsSolvent() (runs: 256, calls: 128000, reverts: 0)","+Suite result: FAILED. 1 passed; 1 failed; 0 skipped; finished in 13.86s (13.86s CPU time)","+```","+","+Every other test in this document is deterministic and reproduces byte-identically.","+","+**Foundry caches failing counterexamples**, so a second run replays the cached one and","+reports `(runs: 0, μ: 0, ~: 0)` instead of a real run count. To make it search afresh:","+","+```bash","+rm -rf cache/fuzz cache/invariant cache/test-failures","+```","+"," ### Files added"," "," | File | Purpose |"]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false}}
